title: On chip, multifunctional quantum sensing using single spins in a van der Waals crystal
authors: James Liddle-Wesolowski, Konosuke Shimazaki, Jiyun Kim, Benjamin Whitefield, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Mehran Kianinia, Igor Aharonovich
abstract: Nanoscale thermometry and magnetometry are in high demand across a wide range of scientific and technological applications. In this context, optically addressable spins in solids have emerged at the forefront of on-chip quantum sensing. However, simultaneous quantum sensing of multiple parameters (e.g., temperature and magnetic field) using the same spin sensor remains challenging due to cross-sensitivity to multiple physical quantities. Here, we demonstrate independent dual sensing of temperature and magnetic field using single quantum emitters in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN). We experimentally verify the independent response of the zero-phonon line (ZPL) position to temperature and of optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) to magnetic fields. Furthermore, we demonstrate local temperature sensing of a microcircuit while simultaneously measuring an external magnetic field. Our results establish quantum emitters in hBN as a robust platform for multifunctional quantum sensing under realistic operating conditions.
summary: The research presents a robust platform for multifunctional quantum sensing using single spins in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN). By independently monitoring the shift of the Zero-Phonon Line (ZPL) with temperature and the Optically Detected Magnetic Resonance (ODMR) frequency with magnetic field, the authors achieve simultaneous, cross-talk-free measurement of both parameters on a chip. This establishes hBN as a promising material for next-generation quantum sensing devices.
main_problem: The challenge of simultaneously measuring multiple physical parameters, such as temperature and magnetic field, using a single quantum spin sensor due to cross-sensitivity.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated independent dual sensing by showing that the Zero-Phonon Line (ZPL) position shifts with temperature while the Optically Detected Magnetic Resonance (ODMR) frequency changes predictably only with the applied magnetic field.
method: They utilized single quantum emitters hosted in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) placed on a chip equipped with an integrated microheating circuit to create controlled thermal gradients, while simultaneously measuring both ZPL and ODMR spectra.
model_or_system:

Figure 2 details the microscale heating circuit fabrication and simulated temperature/magnetic field distributions. Figure 3 characterizes the emitters and shows ZPL vs T fits, while Figure 4 presents the independent thermal (ZPL) and magnetic (ODMR) responses.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the need for multifunctional quantum sensors; it details the experimental setup using hBN on a microheater; it presents measurements showing the distinct temperature dependence of ZPL and the field dependence of ODMR; finally, it demonstrates simultaneous local sensing capability.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the development of solid-state quantum sensors by engineering an environment (hBN/microcircuit) that allows for orthogonal readout channels, which is crucial for building complex quantum measurement devices.
